notes: Corrected one edge: the *of* of *for want of clothing* was moved from בְּלִי to its nomen rectum לְבוּשׁ. בְּלִי is tagged Ncmsc here, so a construct relation stands between the two nouns, and rule 19 places that relation on the rectum; the accepted reading treated *want of* as one indivisible English rendering, which rule 19 explicitly forbids for *all of*, *any of* and *any kind of*. Everything else is unchanged.
The privative division follows rule 48: the מִן keeps the function word *for* and the present negative substantive takes the negation word, rather than the מִן taking both.
*the needy had no covering* divides as rule 43 and rule 50 direct — the possessive לְ carries the *had* and אַיִן heads on *no*.
